title: Duplicate `else if (status === "error")` and `else` branches in handleTrain have byte-identical bodies
description: The two trailing branches of the handleTrain dispatch are identical: `else if (result.status === "error") { useNodeResultsStore.getState().completeTrainJob(nodeId, result as unknown as TrainResult) }` and `else { useNodeResultsStore.getState().completeTrainJob(nodeId, result as unknown as TrainResult) }`. The only difference is the explanatory comment ('Immediate validation error' vs 'Synchronous completion'). Since both the error and the synchronous-completion cases call `completeTrainJob` with exactly the same arguments and no third (terminalStatus) argument, the `else if` predicate is dead — collapsing it into the single `else` is behaviour-preserving and removes a redundant branch. (Distinct from the known configHash="" staleness finding, which concerns store behaviour; this is purely the redundant control flow in the component.)
evidence: Lines 143-145 and 146-149 both execute `useNodeResultsStore.getState().completeTrainJob(nodeId, result as unknown as TrainResult)` with identical args. `parseTrainResponse` restricts `status` to started|completed|error, so the `else` already covers `completed`; merging the error branch into it changes nothing observable.
behavior_preservation: Identical: both branches invoke completeTrainJob(nodeId, result) with the same arguments; merging removes a redundant predicate without changing any call or its arguments.
